title: The 10 Best Instant Pots Under $100
metaDescription: Our 10 picks for instant pots under $100, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at instant pots under $100 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Instant Pot Duo 7-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker 6-Quart
products.blurb: Key specs: 6-quart stainless steel insert, 7-in-1 functions: pressure cook, slow cook, rice, sauté, steam, warm, yogurt, 14 smart programs.
strengths: Sauté function eliminates the need for a separate pan before pressure cooking, real value at this price
Cheap, widely available replacement parts keep long-term ownership costs low
limitations: Dial interface with no digital feedback beyond the timer display
Sealing ring absorbs food odors and needs periodic replacement to stay fresh-smelling
No custom program memory for saving personalized settings
features: 6-quart stainless steel insert
7-in-1 functions: pressure cook, slow cook, rice, sauté, steam, warm, yogurt
14 smart programs
3-ply bottom for even sauté heat

Same loud steam release and dated dial interface as every Duo variant

products.name: Cuisinart CPC-600 6-Quart Electric Pressure Cooker

Cuisinart's brand reputation offers an alternative for buyers who specifically want to avoid the Instant Pot ecosystem
limitations: Smaller recipe ecosystem than Instant Pot means more manual cook-time conversion
Replacement gaskets and sealing rings are harder to source than Instant Pot's widely stocked parts

products.name: Instant Pot Max 6-Quart Electric Pressure Cooker with Sous Vide
products.blurb: Key specs: 6-quart stainless steel insert, 9-in-1 functions including sous vide, pressure can, and sterilize, 15 PSI max pressure, higher than the Duo's 11.6 PSI.
strengths: One of the few models with genuine pressure canning support, a real differentiator most Instant Pot models explicitly warn against
Higher 15 PSI max pressure cuts cook times further on tough cuts, a performance edge at a comparable sale price
Sous vide with tighter temperature control competes with dedicated immersion circulators costing more on their own
limitations: Higher pressure requires more caution with liquid levels, less forgiving for less experienced cooks
Limited availability compared to the actively produced Duo line makes parts sourcing harder
Pressure canning still isn't USDA-endorsed for all low-acid foods, a caveat for serious canners
